authoredFrom: PS11/PS23 — the symbol payload the STORE actually reads. Authored 2026-09-26. `pool-worker.ts` carries a symbol across the worker boundary by NAMING its fields and drops the whole `metadata` object except the narrow `isDeclaration` key. The pre-wave lane wrote `isStatic`, `isHidden`, `annotations`, `type` and `docstring` INTO `metadata`, so every one was discarded before the store saw it — measured at the store: a `static [int]` property stored with `is_static = 0` and `[ValidateSet('a','b')]` stored with `annotations = NULL`, on a project where the analyzer had extracted both. Two shapes are pinned per finding, because each took two attempts: `[CmdletBinding()]` lives on `function_statement > script_block > param_block > attribute_list` (a direct-child read found none, and so did a `param_block`-child read), and a parameter's TYPE is spelled as an attribute, so it sits at `script_parameter > attribute_list > attribute > type_literal` — two levels down, and discriminated from `[Parameter()]`/`[ValidateSet()]` by having a DIRECT `type_literal` child. The docstring channel also pins the ADJACENCY rule: the first scanner skipped blank lines while walking upward and published this file's own banner as `Get-Report`'s documentation.

expectParameters.comment: an UNTYPED parameter reads `untyped`, not `any` — `[int]$d = 0` and `$d = 0` are different contracts and the store's `parameters` JSON is the only place either survives. (This sentence sat inside a `parameters` entry on first authoring; the parameter matcher exempts only `note` and `isNamed`, so a `comment` there is read as a FIELD and the pin could never match. `comment`/`note` are documentation only at the ENTRY level.)

forbidParameters.comment: PRE-FIX SHAPE: the placeholder the pre-wave reader emitted for a parameter whose type it could not read. Because a parameter's type is spelled as an attribute, EVERY typed parameter in the language read `any` — which is the same blind spot the csharp R7 paydown closed family-wide, and the reason `forbidParameters.types` exists at all.

expectDecorators.comment: PS11: the attribute is on the `param_block`, two levels below the function statement. Measured pre-fix: every PowerShell function stored with `annotations = NULL`. It is pinned on the FUNCTION's symbol, not on a parameter: `[CmdletBinding()]` declares the function as an ADVANCED function, and a parameter has its own list.

forbidDecorators.comment: a PowerShell class attribute is NOT a decorator. `static` and `hidden` are bare keywords in the member list — `class_attribute` in the grammar — while a decorator is the bracketed `[...]` form (`[CmdletBinding()]`, `[ValidateSet()]`, `[Parameter()]`). Modelling `static` as a decorator would be the csharp spelling imported into a language that does not have it, and it is pinned here as absent so the two stay distinct. The static-ness is carried by `isStatic`, asserted below.

expectIsStatic.comment: `hidden` is not `static` — a regression that mapped `hidden` onto `isStatic` would satisfy a presence check and fail this

expectReturnType.comment: the declared return type of a class method
a PowerShell function has no declared return type; `any` is the honest value and is distinct from a declared `any`

expectDocstring.comment: PS23: comment-based help IS a PowerShell function's documentation (`about_Comment_Based_Help`). The pre-wave lane read no comment but `#requires`, so `docstring` was `null` for every symbol in the language.

forbidDocstring.comment: the ADJACENCY rule: this file's comment above `enum Level` is a blank line away from `Store`, so it is not `Store`'s documentation. The first scanner skipped blank lines and published the FILE BANNER as the docstring of whichever declaration came first — a resolvable, plausible, wholly wrong row.
and no docstring at all: the file banner belongs to the file, not to a declaration that happens to follow it
